250.h: Edusoko University is a private university established in 2021 and accredited by the National Universities Commission. It describes itself as the first community-based private university in its region, and its stated mission is to empower students through good-quality education and research that drive social progress and inclusive growth.
250.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes that combine theory with practical experience, alongside cultural and extracurricular activities.
250.c: The university is located in Bida, Niger State, in north-central Nigeria.

267.h: Federal University, Kashere (FUK) was one of the federal universities created under a Federal Government plan to widen access to higher education and give every state a fair share of federal institutions. A memorandum at the Federal Executive Council's 39th meeting, on 10 November 2010, proposed 44 new tertiary institutions. The council approved twelve new universities, nine of them, including Kashere, in the first phase. A committee reported on locations and arrangements on 15 November 2010, state governments helped identify permanent and take-off sites, and each university received ₦1.5 billion in start-up funding. The National Universities Commission records the university's establishment in 2011.
267.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
267.c: It is located in Kashere, Gombe State, in north-eastern Nigeria.

277.h: Hallmark University is a private university established by the Vivian Fowler Memorial Trust Foundation, the organisation behind Vivian Fowler Memorial College for Girls in Lagos, and approved by the Federal Government. It began teaching on 1 March 2016, admitting students to its faculties of Natural and Applied Sciences and of Management and Social Sciences. It aims to run programmes relevant to the economic and social development of Nigeria and sub-Saharan Africa.
277.a: The university offers more than 18 degree programmes across the sciences, management and the social sciences. Candidates must be at least 16 years old at the start of the session.
277.c: The campus at Ijebu-Itele, Ogun State, has laboratories, teaching facilities and student residences.

278.h: Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida University, Lapai (IBBUL) is a public university owned by the Niger State Government and named after General Ibrahim Babangida, a former head of state who comes from Niger State. It began academic activities in the 2005/2006 session and held its first convocation in 2014.
278.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. Its Department of History, for example, was set up in September 2006 in the Faculty of Education and Arts and started on the Kobo campus with eleven pioneer students and three teaching staff.
278.c: It is located in Lapai, Niger State, in central Nigeria, with teaching on more than one campus in the town.

279.h: Igbinedion University, Okada is a private university founded by Chief Gabriel Igbinedion, its proprietor and chancellor. Its operating licence, dated 20 April 1999, was presented to him on 10 May 1999, which places it among the first private universities licensed in Nigeria. An implementation committee was formed two days later and was dissolved when the proprietor inaugurated the university's governing council on 14 October 1999. Its first vice-chancellor, Professor Osagie, served from 29 October 1999 to 30 November 2003.
279.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine, law, engineering and health-care administration and hospital management.
279.c: It is located in Okada, a town in Ovia North-East, Edo State. Students live and study on a residential campus.

285.h: Kebbi State University of Science and Technology, Aliero (KSUSTA) is a public university owned by the Kebbi State Government, now renamed Abdullahi Fodio University of Science and Technology, Aliero. It was established in December 2006 by a state law, after the state executive council approved it and the House of Assembly passed the bill. The National Universities Commission licensed it as Nigeria's 79th university, and teaching began in January 2008 with 404 students.
285.a: KSUSTA focuses on agriculture and the sciences, among other programmes. It now has about 8,800 students: around 8,470 undergraduates and 350 postgraduates.
285.c: It is located in Aliero, Kebbi State, in north-western Nigeria.

286.h: Kings University is a private university founded in 2015 by the Kingsway International Christian Centre, the church led by Pastor Matthew Ashimolowo, who serves as the university's chancellor. Its vice-chancellor is Professor Adenike Kuku, a biochemist.
286.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes in several faculties. From the 2023/2024 session the National Universities Commission approved three more programmes in its Faculty of Basic Medical Sciences: nursing science, public health and medical laboratory science.
286.c: It is located at Ode-Omu in Osun State, south-western Nigeria.
